title: Higher Gain Satellite Communication Antenna and Receiver Installation
abstract: A higher gain satellite antenna and a matched receiver are launched to recover link margin on polar and southern ocean sectors, where the delivered installation drops below the contracted availability figure.

sections.reason: Link availability on polar routings and on southern ocean sectors falls below the ninety-eight per cent figure the datalink service is contracted against, with measured losses concentrated above sixty-five degrees latitude where the elevation angle to the satellite is low. Six operators report the same pattern and two have raised it commercially. The cause is antenna gain at low elevation rather than any defect in the installed equipment, so a performance change rather than a reliability fix is needed.
sections.description: The antenna is replaced by a higher gain item with an improved low elevation pattern, and the data unit receiver D2370120510465 is replaced by a matched unit with a lower noise figure. Protective sleeving LN6296K1 is fitted where the coaxial run leaves the pressure boundary, and countersunk screws AES915798K5 hold the revised radome adapter. Arrangement is on drawing D23701188829. Work is on the upper fuselage crown and in the aft cabin ceiling, zones 265 and 212, with the radome removed. The satellite antenna 175RN is replaced and the interface unit 33RC8 is re-cabled. The datalink router and the cabin connectivity installation are not touched.
sections.effects: Estimated mass increase of 6.8 kg per aircraft, high and slightly aft of the reference datum. Electrical load increase of 140 VA. Not interchangeable: the radome adapter and the coaxial run both change. Predicted link availability at high latitude improves from ninety-three to ninety-nine per cent on the modelled routings. Aerodynamic drag increases marginally and is inside the reporting threshold. The antenna installation task and the wiring documentation for the crown route both require reissue.
sections.embodiment_note: Launched for both production and retrofit. Retrofit is a two-shift job with the radome off, so it is offered at a scheduled C-check. Production cut-in will be set once the antenna supplier confirms the qualification test completion date.
sections.open_points: Pre-analysis must confirm that the taller radome adapter stays inside the certified fuselage contour used for the ice shedding assessment, and whether the crown harness route has the spare capacity for the heavier coaxial run.

type_data.balance_impact: Upper fuselage, slightly aft, CG shift below 0.04 % MAC
type_data.production_impact: Cut-in to be set on antenna supplier qualification completion
